- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.9) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — price may not fall as sharply.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — price may not rise as much.
- After a sharp spike in price or sentiment, model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast slope in next 3–5 periods.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines), model often underestimates rebound — increase forecast slightly above recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.9 → -1.5 → +0.9), model misreads momentum — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment swing lag (delayed reaction).
